prerequisites: Practical programming skills in object-oriented programming analogous to the concepts taught in the "Programming 1 (I)" course. Students wishing to refresh programming skills are recommended to participate in a Cloud-based MOOC.

learning_outcomes.text: Students know current database technologies and their application areas.
Students have in-depth knowledge of modeling, normalization, transactions, and a database query language.

Students can model, implement, and query databases. They adhere to established quality-assuring development processes. They are able to critically reflect on their results. Students are practiced in using selected database technologies and can assess their applicability and practical relevance in a situation and domain-specific manner.

Students are able to apply modern and established database technologies as part of complex information technology projects. They can independently learn new database technologies and concepts and incorporate them into practical projects.

Students can present their developed results to a specialist audience within the framework of formal presentations. They are capable of critical technical discussion with colleagues, users, database experts, and software developers.

syllabus_topics: Concepts, architectures and terms of database systems
Database management systems and their foundation
Conceptual and logical data modeling (e.g., ER modeling, table design)
Transformation of modeling to a concrete data model (e.g., from EER to relational)
Normalization, normal forms, redundancy, efficiency aspects
Introduction to a query language (e.g., SQL) including programming language extensions
Use of databases from programming languages

assessment_methods.method: Term paper (approx. 15 pages) with accompanying presentation (approx. 10 minutes)

assessment_rules: The selection of graded and ungraded assessment methods from the given options is at the discretion of the respective lecturer, who adheres to the valid study regulations. For graded assessments, a written exam or a term paper is possible. For ungraded assessments, experimental work or regular participation is possible. For regular participation, attendance of at least 80% of the course is required.
